mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing the closed-world permission matrix fact removes all constraints on which (Relationship, OperationKind) cells are allowed. Injecting a ShareeRel→OpDeleteTask and TeamAdminRel→OpPatchShareList cell forces a counterexample where sharees can delete tasks and admins can hijack share lists — exactly what FR-010/FR-011 forbid.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_RelPermViolation { ShareeRel -> OpDeleteTask in RelPermMatrix.relAllowed  TeamAdminRel -> OpPatchShareList in RelPermMatrix.relAllowed }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing the role permission matrix removes the universal prohibition on OpDeleteAuditEntry and OpUpdateAuditEntry. Injecting TeamAdmin→OpDeleteAuditEntry forces a counterexample where admins can delete audit entries, violating the append-only and immutability assertions.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditMutationViolation { TeamAdmin -> OpDeleteAuditEntry in RolePermMatrix.roleAllowed  TeamAdmin -> OpUpdateAuditEntry in RolePermMatrix.roleAllowed }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing the same-team constraint on sharedWith removes FR-012's enforcement. The injection forces a task to have a sharee from a different team, violating cross-team isolation — a sharee in another team can now reach the task, breaking NoInformationLeakage for the outsider path.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_CrossTeamShareViolation { some t: Task | some u: User | u not in t.sharedWith and u.userTeam != t.taskTeam and u in t.sharedWith }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing the constraint that only the task owner authors Shared/Unshared audit entries removes attribution enforcement. Injecting a Shared audit entry authored by a non-owner (e.g., a sharee user) forces a counterexample where a sharee could generate share audit events, contradicting FR-013 and misattribution.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_ShareAttributionViolation { some ae: AuditEntry | ae.auditOp = Shared and ae.auditActor != ae.auditTask.taskOwner }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing the same-team constraint on audit actors removes the invariant that only in-team users generate audit entries. Injecting an audit entry whose actor is from a different team than the task forces a counterexample violating cross-team isolation as a side-effect of auditing.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_CrossTeamAuditViolation { some ae: AuditEntry | ae.auditActor.userTeam != ae.auditTask.taskTeam }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing the constraint that every task must have a Created audit entry removes the audit-completeness guarantee. Injecting a task with no audit entries at all forces a counterexample where a task exists with no audit record — violating SC-007 (zero observable state changes without a corresponding audit entry).
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_MissingAuditViolation { some t: Task | no ae: AuditEntry | ae.auditTask = t }
